name: Airflow
tagline: Platform to programmatically author, schedule and monitor workflows.
hook: A broad guide to repository structure, commands, security reports, newsfragments, remote naming, and commit rules.
summary: Airflow's file ranges from repository structure and commands to writing and contribution policy. It defines one domain term, classifies security reports, explains newsfragments, fixes remote names, and limits commit trailers.

techniques.title: One word, with its exceptions enumerated
techniques.body: The term uses title case in prose. Literal code tokens keep their original spelling, including inside fenced blocks, and anti-pattern quotes may show the wrong form when teaching the rule.
techniques.quote:
Write **Dag** (title case) in all prose. Keep the all-caps or lowercase
spelling only when reproducing a literal code token — never rewrite these,
even inside fenced code blocks

techniques.title: How to classify a security finding
techniques.body: The guide separates security findings into vulnerabilities, known limitations, and deployment hardening. It links the security model, including the chapter that defines what is not a vulnerability.

techniques.title: Open the pull request, not the issue
techniques.body: When the fix is known, open a pull request instead of an issue. The pull request already holds the title, description, diff, and discussion, while an issue can attract duplicate fixes. A deferred fix still needs an issue that outlives the workaround.
techniques.quote:
Open issues attract drive-by submissions, often from other agents, that
  haven't seen the in-flight work.

techniques.title: Deferred work linked from the code
techniques.body: A workaround, version cap, or partial fix needs a tracking issue before the pull-request body is final. Reference its number in the pull request and put the full URL beside the workaround, where a bare issue number would not resolve.

techniques.title: No agent co-author trailer
techniques.body: The commit section ends with a line prohibiting the agent from adding itself as a co-author, with the stated distinction that agents are assistants rather than authors. A separate PR template field discloses the agent by name and version instead.
techniques.quote: NEVER add Co-Authored-By with yourself as co-author of the commit. Agents cannot be authors, humans can be, Agents are assistants.

techniques.title: Remote names checked rather than assumed
techniques.body: Two remote names are fixed by convention. The agent is told to run git remote -v before any remote command, and where the names do not match, to surface the mismatch and propose the exact rename commands rather than silently working with what is there.

techniques.title: A coverage target with an upper bound
techniques.body: Tests are to cover exactly what the PR changes: every changed behavior gets a test, every test must fail without the change, and tests for pre-existing logic or third-party functions are excluded.
techniques.quote: Target exactly 100% coverage of what the PR changes — no more, no less.

steal: If your project has a term people spell three ways, fix the spelling and enumerate the exceptions.
Tell agents how to classify a security finding, including which categories not to report.
State whether an agent may add itself as a commit co-author.
Before any remote command, have the agent verify remote names rather than assume them.
"Every test must fail without the change" is a sharper instruction than a coverage percentage.
